    Bar snacksBorder town street tacosSlow-roasted chilli pork crisped in a pan, with pineapple, onion and corianderHow to make it800g pork shoulder3 dried chillies2 oranges200g fresh pineapple, plus extra to serve12 small corn tortillas1 small white onion1 bunch coriander2 cloves of garlicflaky salt, to tasteSoak the dried chillies in hot water, then blitz with orange juice, some pineapple and garlic to a smooth marinade.Coat the pork in the marinade, season and rub in well.Roast the pork covered at 160°C until it pulls apart.Shred or slice the pork and crisp it in a very hot pan.Warm the tortillas and serve with diced pineapple, onion and coriander.Charred jalapeño guacamole and chipsSmashed avocado with charred jalapeño, lime, onion and corianderHow to make it2 jalapenos3 ripe avocados2 limes1/2 white onion1 handful coriander50g feta1 bag corn chipssalt, to tasteChar the jalapenos in a dry pan until blackened, then seed and chop fine.Smash the avocados roughly with a fork.Stir through the jalapeno, lime juice, onion and coriander, then season well.Top with crumbled feta.Warm the corn chips at 180°C and serve straight away.Cantina garlic and chilli fried peanutsToasted with garlic, lime and salt at Dominó's bar, where she keeps a letter-opener handyHow to make itNot on tonight's cookRaw peanuts fried with whole garlic cloves and dried chillies until golden, tossed hot with lime and salt, served by the bowl on the bar.Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide pan over medium heat.Add 400g raw peanuts and 8 peeled garlic cloves and stir for 6 minutes until golden.Add 6 dried red chillies broken in half and cook 1 more minute.Tip into a bowl, squeeze over a lime and toss with 1 tsp salt and a pinch of chilli powder.Cool for 10 minutes so they crisp up before serving.Ceviche tostadasThe bartender already has a full band.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.PlatesMoco's carne asadaLime and cumin skirt steak, rice and beans. Save a scrap for Dominó's pit bullHow to make it800g skirt steak2 limes1 orange4 cloves of garlic2 tsp ground cumin300g long grain rice400g can black beans1 bunch spring onionssalt, to tasteMix lime juice, a little orange juice, crushed garlic, cumin and a good pinch of salt, then add the steak.Marinate the steak at room temperature for 2 hours.Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, and warm the beans in a small pot.Sear the steak over very high heat for 3 minutes a side, char the spring onions in the same pan.Rest the steak, then slice thin against the grain.Serve with the rice, beans and spring onions.Red chilli chicken enchiladasShredded chicken and cheese in corn tortillas, baked bubbling under crema, for the hotel shootoutHow to make itNot on tonight's cookCorn tortillas rolled around shredded chicken and cheese, covered in a red chilli and tomato sauce and more cheese, baked bubbling and finished with crema and coriander.Poach 600g chicken thighs in salted water for 20 minutes, then shred.Soak 3 dried chillies in hot water, then blitz with a 400g can of tomatoes, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin and salt, and simmer 10 minutes.Dip 8 corn tortillas in the sauce, fill with chicken and 150g grated cheddar, roll and pack into a dish.Pour over the rest of the sauce, top with 100g more cheese and bake at 190°C for 20 minutes.Finish with sour cream and coriander.AftersCocadas, coconut condensed milk bitesBaked coconut mounds, for the free coconut at the edge of townHow to make it250g desiccated coconut395g sweetened condensed milk2 egg yolks1 tsp vanilla extractMix the coconut, condensed milk, egg yolks and vanilla.Spoon 20 small mounds onto a lined tray.Bake at 170°C until golden on the edges.Cool on the tray until firm.Behind the barMixed-up guitar case michelada beerLager, lime, tomato juice, hot sauce. Azul wants his in a bottle.How to make it4 bottles of Mexican lager4 limes250ml tomato juice2 tbsp salt1 tsp chilli powder1 tsp hot sauce2 tsp Worcestershire sauce1 bag iceMix the salt and chilli powder on a plate.Run a lime wedge around four tall glasses and dip the rims in the chilli salt.Fill the glasses with ice.Add lime juice, tomato juice, hot sauce and Worcestershire sauce to each glass.Top with cold lager, stir once and garnish with a lime wedge.Agua de jamaicaSlow sipping, like the turtle on the highway.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
